subject: person sneezing
title: A Single Sneeze Can Carry Droplets 27 Feet Across a Room

scenes.text: Standing six feet from a sneeze? You're nowhere near out of range.
High-speed cameras at MIT filmed sneezes, and the droplets kept going.
One sneeze threw them twenty-three to twenty-seven feet. That's seven to eight meters.
Why so far? The droplets don't fly alone. They ride a warm, wet cloud of gas.
That cloud keeps them from drying out, so they drift instead of dropping.
The six-foot rule came from a 1930s idea of lone droplets. It covers about a quarter of a sneeze.

description:
MIT researcher Lydia Bourouiba filmed sneezes with high-speed cameras: the droplets travel 23 to 27 feet (7 to 8 meters).
They ride a warm, moist, turbulent cloud of gas that keeps them from evaporating and carries them far beyond the roughly 2 meters predicted by a 1930s model of lone droplets.
How far away do you stand when someone sneezes?
